transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC | 60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (CISO - Helix), Priya Nair (Head of Platform), Liam Chen (Ops), Ava Brooks (Sec Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Alright thanks everyone for joining, I'll kick us off. This is Jordan from Redwood, with Maya our solutions engineer. Today we wanted to walk through audit logs and admin activity, what we capture, how you can export, retention, and encryption options.
[00:18] Sam: Sounds good, thanks. High level our ask is we need to understand what events we get out of the box, how reliably they're timestamped and attributed, and options for exporting to our SIEM and long-term storage for compliance.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Quick agenda — capture surface, delivery/export, retention/archival, encryption/KMS, and then RBAC and attribution. Also we'll flag any gaps for SOC2/ISO.
[00:45] Priya: One note — our security/compliance team requires 7 years for some payment-related artifacts, so curious about archival to S3 or cold storage.
[00:55] Maya: Yep we'll cover archival.

[02:10] Maya: First, what we capture: admin actions (role changes, user invites, SSO config changes), authentication events (login success/fail, token use), API key lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke), model deploys and route changes, exports/downloads, and system-level operations like node reboots in dedicated clusters. Our internal field names are slightly different — we export as JSONL with event_type, actor_id, actor_email, timestamp_iso, target_resource, action, outcome, request_id.
[02:40] Liam: Are there events for data access — like which user queried embeddings or fetched a model endpoint with PII?
[02:50] Maya: We emit request-level metadata including request_id and route. We don't log full prompt text by default for hosted mode — prompt capture is opt-in and can be redacted. For dedicated/private you can configure logging of request payloads.
[03:10] Sam: So for hosted we get meta, for dedicated we can get payloads if we opt in. Any masking options?
[03:20] Maya: Yes we have redaction hooks and automatic PII filters, plus configurable retention for payloads.

[05:00] Jordan: On attribution — we support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, so events will map to your directory identities when you enable SAML. If you don't provision via SCIM, the actor might be an API key owner which shows as a service principal.
[05:20] Ava: How granular is the actor trace? We need to show both the human who initiated the API key creation and downstream service usages for audits.
[05:30] Maya: We include creator_id on key create events and then each request shows the key_id used. You can correlate creator_id -> key_id. We also attach session ids where available. There can be some timing mismatch but generally it's one-to-one.

[07:10] Priya: Export options? We use Splunk and BigQuery, but prefer S3 landing zone as canonical archive.
[07:20] Maya: Primary options: push to your S3 bucket (server-side encrypted or SSE-KMS), BigQuery via push or GCS, direct SIEM connectors (Splunk/Datadog) via forwarders, webhooks for real-time events, and Kafka/syslog for streaming. Exports are batched (1–5 minute windows) but we can drop to near-real-time for critical ops.
[07:45] Sam: For S3, do you support CMEK (customer-managed keys) or only Redwood-managed?
[07:55] Maya: We support CMEK for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we offer SSE-KMS with Redwood-managed keys and an enterprise option for CMEK with a key rotation SLA. For on-prem/private you can integrate with your HSM.

[09:30] Liam: What about integrity — can we detect tampering? We need chain-of-custody for audit.
[09:40] Maya: We provide signed manifests per export batch with hash digests (SHA256) and timestamped manifests. For Dedicated we can ship logs to an append-only store or provide signed event streams. We also support object lock on S3 for immutability if you want write-once storage.

[11:00] Sam: Retention defaults and per-tenant config? We want short-term hot logs for 90 days and long-term cold archive for 7 years. Need cost estimates.
[11:10] Jordan: Default retention in Hosted is 90 days for audit logs; you can configure log export to your S3 for long-term retention. Pricing for archival depends on storage destination — we provide guidance and a calculator. For Dedicated you can set retention policy centrally and we can assist with lifecycle rules to move to glacier or equivalent.

[13:00] Priya: Can you filter events before export? We don't want PII to land in analytics buckets.
[13:10] Maya: Yes — export filters by event_type or by explicit field rules. You can redact fields at export time or use server-side transform lambda to scrub. We recommend redaction before landing.

[15:20] Ava: On encryption in transit — do exports go over TLS? What about signing?
[15:25] Maya: All exports use TLS 1.2/1.3. For S3 we recommend SSE-KMS; we sign the manifests. For webhook deliveries we support mutual TLS and HMAC signatures per payload.

[17:40] Sam: For compliance, we need to tie events to roles and show RBAC changes, e.g., who promoted someone to admin and when. Does the audit include both the request and the policy delta?
[17:50] Maya: Role assignment events include before/after snapshots for critical changes and we capture the policy id and version. The event payload includes previous_roles and new_roles when available. There might be slight differences in older logs but current schema includes the delta.

[20:10] Jordan: Quick note on SIEM integration — we have a mapping doc for Splunk sourcetypes and for Datadog logs ingestion so you can map our event_type to your fields. We'll share those.

[22:00] Priya: Are there searchable fields for retention queries? Like query by actor_email or request_id across months?
[22:10] Maya: If you ingest to BigQuery or Splunk you can index as needed and run long-range queries. Our native console search supports 90-day windows in Hosted; for longer windows we recommend external warehousing.

[24:30] Liam: About rate/throughput — if we export all request-level events from peak traffic, will the export pipeline keep up? We do production peaks that are large.
[24:40] Maya: We autoscale export workers and support batching; for very high-throughput customers we offer a direct Kafka stream or dedicated export links for higher throughput SLAs. For Dedicated you can put in a throughput commit as part of the reserved capacity.

[27:00] Sam: Any gaps you see for Helix specifically?
[27:10] Maya: From what you've described, main items are: you need per-event payload retention for 7 years (we can archive to S3), you want CMEK for exported objects (supported in Dedicated/Private and enterprise hosted option), and you want signed manifests for chain-of-custody (we provide that). We'll need your event list so we can confirm no missing event types.

[29:00] Priya: About prompt logging and PII — we have regulated data, we want minimal exposure. If we go Dedicated/private, can we run all logging internal-only?
[29:12] Maya: Yes Dedicated and Private allow internal-only logging and full control over retention and redaction. Hosted can be configured but certain deep payloads are opt-in.

[31:00] Jordan: Questions on PKI/KMS: we support KMS integrations and HSM for Private. Key rotation policies are supported and logged as key_rotate events. We can also do envelope encryption if you want double-wrapping.
[31:25] Ava: Do you log key usage? We need to know who used a key and when.
[31:30] Maya: Yes key_use events are emitted; they include key_id, principal, and purpose. We also include key rotation and revoke events.

[33:50] Sam: Are you SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified? We need to review the report and controls mapping.
[33:58] Jordan: We are SOC2 Type II and working on ISO; I'll share the latest report and the controls mapping to audit log capabilities.

[35:10] Priya: On identity: SCIM provisioning — can we automatically keep groups and role mappings in sync so that event attribution uses our AD groups?
[35:20] Maya: Yes SCIM provisioning supports group->role mappings; events will include group IDs and role names. We also support SAML assertions mapping where your IdP provides role attributes.

[37:00] Liam: For legal hold or e-discovery, can you support on-demand export for a given user or request_id range?
[37:10] Maya: We allow ad-hoc exports via the console or API filtered by request_id, actor_email, time range. For large exports we recommend using BigQuery/GCS flows.

[40:00] Sam: A few edge-case Qs — how are service disruptions logged? If a node is taken out or fallback occurs, is that captured?
[40:10] Maya: We log system events, autoscale adjustments, failovers, model fallback, and their timestamps. We include correlated request_ids when possible.

[43:00] Jordan: Recap and gaps: we'll send SOC2 report, the audit log schema, and Splunk/Datadog mapping. Maya will spin up an S3 export for the PoC. Helix will provide the event list and retention policy. Pricing/archival calculator will follow.

[44:15] Sam: One concern — we use an external SIEM and don't want raw payloads with customer PII. We'll likely want redaction + hashing of identifiers.
[44:30] Maya: Agreed — redaction pipeline recommended. We can configure transform lambda pre-ingest into your bucket and we can support hashing of user identifiers.

[46:00] Priya: Anything about audit log access controls? We need RBAC to ensure only auditors and security have read access to long-term logs.
[46:10] Maya: Access control is via RBAC and you can bind read-only roles to an audit group. For exported buckets you control IAM; we also support signed URLs and limited-time access tokens if you need temporary access.

[48:30] Ava: For immutability, you mentioned S3 object lock — is that something Redwood configures or we must set on our bucket?
[48:40] Maya: For Hosted you can have Redwood write into our managed bucket with object lock enabled as an enterprise option; for customer-owned S3 buckets you set the object lock/lifecycle rules and we will honor it.

[50:00] Jordan: Any final questions?
[50:10] Sam: No final questions, main next steps are SOC2, sample logs, and PoC.

[51:00] Jordan: Great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and the PoC invite.

[51:10] Maya: I'll send the export manifest and sample JSONL and a link to the Splunk mapping doc.
[51:20] Priya: Thanks all.

End transcript.

Notes: Transcript has occasional imperfect attribution and minor transcription errors (e.g., K V cache noted elsewhere in other calls). References shared: Splunk mapping doc link (link withheld), SOC2 report (to be sent), sample JSONL manifest (to be provided).
